scope_allowed: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

models.name: M1: Stent-only implicit FEA
models.what_it_computes: Elastoplastic stress–strain response of the stent lattice through crimping, balloon expansion, recoil, and subsequent loading; local mean and alternating stress for fatigue safety factor; radial resistive force under uniform compression.

models.name: M2: Stent–artery implicit FEA
models.what_it_computes: Coupled contact mechanics of the stent with a hyperelastic anisotropic arterial wall and plaque analog; post-deployment residual field, contact pressures, stress amplification, and radial support with host-artery constraint effects.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism A: Deployment residual strains
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sets the mean stress and plastic strain from which fatigue cycles initiate and determines immediate post-deployment margin to yielding.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism B: Pulsatile fatigue
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Cyclic pressure and curvature drive alternating stresses that govern lifetime and risk of strut fracture.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism C: Acute radial strength
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Quasi-static uniform radial compression establishes support against vessel recoil and external crush.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported per model–mechanism on a 0–7 Credibility Index with mechanism-specific acceptance thresholds; matrices of scores are presented without mapping to standard ordinal levels.

expected_decision.outcome_source: With these results, both models are accepted for use within the CoU as follows.

expected_context_of_use: The intended use of the models is to support nonclinical design verification by predicting two classes of performance: (a) fatigue safety factor under ISO 25539-2 pulsatile pressure cycling with an imposed cyclic curvature representative of the coronary environment, and (b) acute radial strength under quasi-static uniform compression.

spans: Input variability within documented manufacturing and measurement tolerances produced output shifts up to 6.5% (A), ±0.14 in fatigue safety factor (B), and 6.0% in radial support (C) for M1; corresponding maxima for M2 were 8.3%, ±0.21, and 7.5%.
findings.span: Input variability within documented manufacturing and measurement tolerances produced output shifts up to 6.5% (A), ±0.14 in fatigue safety factor (B), and 6.0% in radial support (C) for M1; corresponding maxima for M2 were 8.3%, ±0.21, and 7.5%.

spans: The average recoil was 5.1% (SD 0.4%).
The M1 model predicted 4.8% recoil (bias 0.3 percentage points), with RMS error 6% on the P–D curve over 8–16 atm.

Validation comparisons showed recoil biases within 0.3 to 0.4 percentage points and pressure–diameter root-mean-square (RMS) error below 6% (M1) and 5% (M2); fatigue alternating-stress margins of 28% (M1) and 20% (M2) relative to runout thresholds with zero fractures in 10-specimen 400 million-cycle tests; and radial compression curve RMS differences within 7% (M1) and 9% (M2).
findings.span: The average recoil was 5.1% (SD 0.4%).
